If we look at the files in ``spec/support/fixtures/approvals/``, all of them are ``.approved`` except for this one which has both an ``.approved`` and a ``.received`` file.

![fixtures](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9089551/63643372-46b9dc80-c6a5-11e9-9dc5-c3bf431fdab4.png)

According to the [github page for approvals](https://github.com/kytrinyx/approvals):

```
If the contents of the received file is to your liking, you can approve the file by renaming it.

mv my_spec.received.txt my_spec.approved.txt
```

This probably means that at some point ``spec/support/fixtures/approvals/liquid_tweet_tag_spec.received.html`` was approved, renamed, but was not removed from git history.

If we look at [the source code for Approvals.verify](https://github.com/kytrinyx/approvals/blob/7977db195ac062625d6a43ed9f4ef32c8e71896a/lib/approvals/approval.rb#L41), it creates a ``.received`` file from an object, looks for an ``.approved`` file, check if they match, and then deletes the ``.received`` if the match is successful, so this seems to be the expected behaviour. 

The correct thing to do here would be to actually **delete this file and commit the changes**.

## Description

**Removes temporary file `` spec/support/fixtures/approvals/liquid_tweet_tag_spec.received.html`` from git history.** 

When running Approval tests, a ``my_spec.received`` file is created and compared to a ``my_spec.approved`` file. If no such ``my_spec.approved`` file exists, the created ``my_spec.received`` file is manually approved by renaming it to ``my_spec.approved``. 

Once this is done, each call to [Approvals.verify](https://github.com/kytrinyx/approvals/blob/7977db195ac062625d6a43ed9f4ef32c8e71896a/lib/approvals/approval.rb#L41) creates a new ``.received`` file from an in-memory object, treats it as temporary and deletes it once it's successfully compared to its respective ``.approved`` file.

The file `` liquid_tweet_tag_spec.received.html`` has already been approved in the past, as ``liquid_tweet_tag_spec.approved.html`` exists. So whenever we run ``rspec spec/liquid_tags/tweet_tag_spec.rb`` the ``liquid_tweet_tag_spec.received.html`` file gets deleted because it was not supposed to be there.
